name: Hyderabadi Biryani
description: Dum-cooked rice layered with marinated meat, saffron, fried onions, and kewra water. Cooked in a sealed handi for 2–3 hours.

name: Kerala Sadya
description: A 26-course vegetarian feast served on banana leaf — includes rice, avial, sambar, rasam, payasam, and pickles.

name: Rajasthani Dal Baati Churma
description: Hard wheat rolls baked in charcoal (baati) served with five-lentil dal and sweet crumbled churma. A desert survival food turned delicacy.

name: Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)
description: Invented accidentally by Kundan Lal Gujral at Moti Mahal in 1948 by adding butter and tomato to leftover tandoori chicken. Now India's most globally recognizable dish.

name: Pani Puri (Golgappa)
description: Hollow crisp wheat balls filled with spiced potato/chickpea and dunked in tangy tamarind-mint water. Enjoyed as street food across India under different names.

name: Masala Dosa
description: A fermented rice-lentil crepe filled with spiced potato masala, served with coconut chutney and sambar. Originated in Udupi and now a nationwide breakfast staple.

name: Chole Bhature
description: Fluffy deep-fried bread (bhature) paired with spiced chickpea curry. A Delhi street institution, best enjoyed at Sitaram Diwan Chand in Paharganj.

name: Rogan Josh
description: A Kashmiri lamb curry slow-cooked with whole spices, dried Kashmiri chillies (for colour without excessive heat), and yogurt. Originally a Persian dish adapted by Kashmiri Pandits.

name: Gulab Jamun
description: Soft milk-solid balls soaked in rose-cardamom sugar syrup. Descended from the Persian luqmat al-qadi, brought to India by Mughal cooks.

name: Vada Pav
description: Mumbai's unofficial street food — spiced mashed potato fritter (vada) in a bread roll (pav) with multiple chutneys. Invented in 1966 near Dadar station.

name: Litti Chokha
description: Whole wheat balls stuffed with roasted gram flour and spices, cooked in cow dung fire, served with roasted eggplant and tomato chokha.

name: Rasogolla
description: Soft spongy balls of cottage cheese (chhena) cooked in light sugar syrup. Invented by Nobin Chandra Das in Kolkata in 1868. Holds a GI tag as a Bengali product.
